inventionTitles.title: 基于人工智能/机器学习的随机接入过程
Random access procedure based on artificial intelligence/machine learning

address.address1: Beijing Jianyuan Shijia Intellectual Property Agency (General Partnership)

section.content: Apparatus and methods for random access for Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) based wireless communications are provided herein. The present disclosure provides an apparatus that includes interface circuitry, and processor circuitry coupled with the interface circuitry. The processor circuitry is to transmit a physical random channel (PRACH) preamble through the interface circuitry, receive a Random Access Response (RAR) through the interface circuitry, transmit a first message through the interface circuitry, wherein the first message includes a first field and a report, wherein the first field is to indicate whether the report is a predicted beam report based on a prediction of an AI/ML model or a measured beam report based on a measurement, and receive a second message through the interface circuitry. Other embodiments are also disclosed and claimed.

本文提供了用于基于人工智能(AI)/机器学习(ML)的无线通信的随机接入的装置和方法。本公开提供了一种装置，其包括接口电路系统；以及与接口电路系统耦合的处理器电路系统。处理器电路系统用于：通过接口电路系统发送物理随机信道(PRACH)前导码；通过接口电路系统接收随机接入响应(RAR)；通过接口电路系统发送第一消息，其中，第一消息包括第一字段和报告，其中第一字段用于指示报告是基于AI/ML模型的预测的预测波束报告，还是基于测量的测量波束报告；以及通过接口电路系统接收第二消息。还公开并要求保护了其它实施例。

Random access procedure based on artificial intelligence/machine learningPriority

The present application is based on and claims priority from U.S. provisional patent application serial No. 63/746,769 filed on month 1 of 2025, the entire disclosure of which is incorporated herein by reference.

Technical Field

Embodiments of the present disclosure relate generally to wireless communications, and more particularly, to an apparatus and method for an artificial intelligence (ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AI)/machine learning (MACHINE LEARNING, ML) based random access procedure.

Background

With the steady advancement and rapid propagation of artificial intelligence (ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AI)/machine learning (MACHINE LEARNING, ML), AI/ML may enter each layer of the communications ecosystem. Future mobile communication systems may act as AI infrastructure capable of providing services for intelligent applications. More fundamentally, AI-based air interface design and distributed computing and intelligent air interface energization would allow for end-to-end native AI and fusion of communications and computing.

For communication systems, high-band communication has attracted considerable attention in the industry because it provides a wide bandwidth to support future integrated communication systems. Beamforming is a key technique for implementing high-band systems because the gain of beamforming can compensate for severe path loss, improve signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and expand coverage.

Detailed Description

Various aspects of the exemplary embodiments will be described using terms commonly employed by those skilled in the art to convey the substance of the disclosure. However, it will be apparent to one skilled in the art that many alternative embodiments may be practiced using some of the described aspects and that the alternative embodiments may be practiced without the specific details. In other instances, well-known features may have been omitted or simplified in order not to obscure the illustrative embodiments.

Furthermore, various operations will be described as multiple discrete operations in turn, in a manner that is most helpful in understanding the exemplary embodiments, however, the order of description should not be construed as to imply that these operations are necessarily order dependent. In particular, these operations need not be performed in the order of presentation.

The expressions "in an embodiment", "in one embodiment", and "in some embodiments" are used repeatedly herein. These expressions generally do not refer to the same embodiment, but may refer to the same embodiment. The terms "comprising," "having," and "including" are synonymous, unless the context dictates otherwise. The expression "A, B or C" and "A/B/C" means "(A), (B), (C), (A and B), (A and C), (B and C) or (A, B and C)".

Fig. 1 shows an example of a 4-step RACH procedure defined in Release-15, rel-15, release 15, 3GPP NR. At 100, the UE may transmit a random access preamble on a Physical Random Access Channel (PRACH) of an Uplink (UL), allowing a 5G base station (gndb, gNB) to estimate a delay between the gNB and the UE for subsequent UL timing adjustment. At 102, the gNB feeds back a random access response (random access response, RAR) that may carry timing reservation (TIMING ADVANCE, TA) command information and UL authentication for the next UL transmission (Tx). At 104, after adjusting the UL timing, the UE transmits Msg3 on a Physical Uplink SHARED CHANNEL (PUSCH) based on UL authentication in the RAR. At 106, the gNB transmits Msg4 for contention resolution.

For the 4-step RACH procedure, coverage enhancement is critical to the correct operation of the system, given that random access is the first step in the UE's access to the network. In general, using a wide beam transmission synchronization signal block (synchronization signal block, SSB) enables coverage of a wider range of UEs. The wide beam is also used to transmit Msg2 and Msg4.

To improve random access performance including 2-step or 4-step RACH, AI/ML based beam acquisition may be used, where a UE or a gNB may predict a beam forming direction with a narrow beam. In this case, some mechanism needs to be defined to implement the AI/ML-based random access procedure.

The following embodiments relate to AI/ML based random access procedures. In particular, embodiments relate to at least one or more of the following:

indication based on AI/ML random access procedure

AI/ML-based random access procedure at UE side

AI/ML based random access procedure for network

Note that while many of the following embodiments and examples are described with reference to an "initial access procedure," such descriptions may additionally/alternatively be used for a "random access procedure," i.e., not only for UEs in the rrc_idle state, but also for UEs in the rrc_inactive state and the rrc_connected state.

Indication based on AI/ML random access procedure

In an embodiment, separate PRACH resources can be configured to indicate whether the UE supports AI/ML based random access procedures. In particular, separate PRACH occasions (PRACH occasions, RO) or separate preambles (in case of shared RO) can be configured by higher layers via system information (systeminformation, SI) (e.g., via remaining minimum system information (REMAINING MINIMUM SYSTEMINFORMATION, RMSI), other system information defined in NR (other systeminformation, OSI)) or dedicated radio resource control (radio resource control, RRC) signaling for AI/ML random access procedures. This may apply to a 2-step RACH procedure and/or a 4-step RACH procedure.

In an example, separate PRACH resources can be used to indicate that the UE supports AI/ML based random access procedures.

In another example, separate PRACH resources can be used to indicate that one or more models are available at the UE side for (a) a set of configured beams for measurement, (b) a set of configured candidate beams for transmission/reception of one or more messages associated with the random access procedure, and thereafter, until the UE receives any further reconfiguration/indication.

In an embodiment, an explicit indication (e.g., a field) may be included in Msg3 for a 4-step RACH procedure or MsgA PUSCH for a 2-step RACH procedure to indicate whether AI/ML based random access procedures are supported.

In one example, an explicit indication may be 1 bit, where a bit of "1" may indicate support and a bit of "0" may indicate no support. In the latter case, this may mean that a random access procedure not based on AI/ML follows, or that a conventional random access procedure follows.

In another example, an explicit indication may be used to indicate that the UE supports AI/ML based random access procedures.

In another example, for an AI/ML based random access procedure using a UE side model, the explicit indication may indicate that one or more models are available at the UE side for (a) a set of configured beams for measurement, (b) a set of configured candidate beams for transmission/reception of one or more messages associated with the random access procedure, and thereafter, until the UE receives any further reconfiguration/indication.

In another example, information identifying the AI/ML model is included in Msg3 for a 4-step RACH procedure, or MsgA PUSCH for a 2-step RACH procedure. The base station uses this information to retrieve meta-information corresponding to the AI/ML model. The meta-information may include a training data set associated with the AI/ML model.

In an embodiment, a field may be included in the RAR for the 4-step RACH procedure and/or in the success RAR (successRAR) or backoff RAR (fallbackRAR) for the 2-step RACH procedure to indicate whether the AI/ML based random access procedure is applied.

In one example, a one-bit field may be included, where a bit of "1" may indicate that an AI/ML-based random access procedure is applied, and a bit of "0" may indicate that an AI/ML-based random access procedure is not applied. In the latter case, this may indicate that a random access procedure other than AI/ML based is applied, or that a conventional random access procedure is applied.

In another example, when an AI/ML based random access procedure is applied, the UE may need to send a predicted beam report according to the AI/ML model on the UE side in Msg3 or MsgA PUSCH, or a measured beam report in Msg3 or MsgA PUSCH. Furthermore, when the AI/ML based random access procedure is applied, the UE may not include the predicted beam report or the measured beam report in Msg3 or MsgA PUSCH.

Further, this may be for physical Downlink (DL) channels/signals, which may include physical downlink shared channels (physical downlink SHARED CHANNEL, PDSCH) and/or physical downlink control channels (physical downlink control channel, PDCCH), and/or may be for physical UL channels/signals, which may include PUSCH and/or physical uplink control channels (physical uplink control channel, PUCCH).

In an embodiment, a set of synchronization and broadcast signals constitutes a measurement reference signal (REFERENCE SIGNALS, RS), also denoted as beam set B for AI/ML model.

In an embodiment, a set of downlink RSs, such as channel state information reference signals (CHANNEL STATE information REFERENCE SIGNALS, CSI-RS), may be configured cell-specifically to the UE as a beam set a, which may be used as a candidate beam set from which the AI/ML model predicts, the predicted beam or beams are used to transmit/receive one or more messages that are part of the random access procedure, and thereafter until the UE receives any further reconfiguration/indication.

In one example, CSI-RS is configured as periodic CSI-RS resources via SIB signaling in a cell-specific manner. In yet another example, the periodicity of at least some CSI-RS resources may be much larger than the SSB periodicity.

In an embodiment, a set of downlink reference signals (e.g., CSI-RS) may be provided to a UE using dedicated RRC signaling of an RRC Release (RRC-Release) message component, and during random access when a subsequent UE is in an rrc_inactive state, beams associated with these CSI-RS resources are interpreted as containing beam set a. The beam set a is used as a candidate beam set from which the AI/ML model predicts, the predicted beam or beams are used to transmit/receive one or more messages as part of the random access procedure, and thereafter until the UE receives any further reconfiguration/indication.

In one example, CSI-RS is configured as periodic CSI-RS resources in a cell-specific manner through SIB signaling. In a further example, the periodicity of at least some of the CSI-RS resources may be much greater than the SSB periodicity.

In one embodiment, the set of synchronization and broadcast signals constituting the inferential reference signal is also denoted as beam set a, which is used as a candidate beam set from which the AI/ML model predicts, the predicted beam or beams are used for transmitting/receiving one or more messages as part of the random access procedure, and thereafter until the UE receives any further reconfiguration/indication.

In one example, a subset of the synchronization and broadcast signal set is denoted as beam set B and is used at the UE for measurements as input to the UE-side or network-side AI/ML model.

In an embodiment, the BS includes information determining availability of one or more AI/ML models in the information broadcast of a specific cell. Such information may include at least the configuration of the measurement set (beam set B) for inputting the AI/ML model and the candidate beam set (beam set a) from which the prediction is output as the AI/ML model.

In an example, information related to AI/ML capability requirements is included in an information broadcast from a specific cell of a BS. In such cells, AI/ML reasoning-enabled UEs with matching AI/ML models may perform AI/ML reasoning during random access.

In an embodiment, the BS includes information identifying the AI/ML model in the paging message broadcast.

In one example, information related to AI/ML capability requirements is included in a paging message from the BS. In such cells, AI/ML reasoning-enabled UEs with matching AI/ML models may perform AI/ML reasoning during random access.

In an embodiment, if the DL transmission (Tx) beam for the transmission configuration indicator (transmission configurationindicator, TCI) status update indication received by Msg4 or MsgB is not included in the beam set used for measurement (i.e., beam set B), then an aperiodic DL RS (e.g., aperiodic CSI-RS resources) may be triggered by a downlink control information (downlink control information, DCI) format, which may schedule PDSCH using Msg4 or MsgB. In this case, the DCI format for scheduling may be conveyed by a physical downlink control channel (physical downlink control channel, PDCCH) and may indicate a first aperiodic CSI-RS transmission followed by a PDSCH (symbols without overlap between PDCCH, CSI-RS and PDSCH). Thus, the UE can activate the corresponding TCI state using CSI-RS before receiving PDSCH. Thus, the timing relationship between the aperiodic CSI-RS and the Msg4 PDSCH, or the timing relationship between the aperiodic CSI-RS and MsgB should ensure that the UE has time to perform CSI-RS reception and TCI state activation before PDSCH reception.

Alternatively, all candidate beams (i.e., in beam set a) may be considered available for indication during random access.

In an embodiment, the maximum duration of the contention resolution window may be extended for AI/ML based random access. For both the UE side and network side models, this may allow for any consideration of TCI state activation prior to applying the model. Further, for the network side model, extending the contention resolution window length may help to accommodate BS processing time, which is necessary to apply model reasoning based on measurement beam reports sent by the UE in Msg3 or MsgA.

AI/ML-based random access procedure at UE side

In an embodiment, the higher layer can configure DL RS resources via system information messages (e.g., OSI defined in RMSI, NR) or via dedicated RRC signaling for AI/ML based random access. The DL RS resource set may include a plurality of DL RS resources and/or SSBs. The DL RS resource may be CSI-RS. The DL RS resource set may be referred to as beam set a for AI/ML based random access procedures. The DL RS resource may be SSB.

In an example, unless already configured as part of beam set B, for example, the UE may not consider DL RS associated with beam set a to be transmitted by the BS and may be used for measurements by the UE in RRC idle or RRC inactive state prior to or during random access.

Fig. 2 shows the following steps, one or more of which may be included in an AI/ML based random access procedure for a 4-step RACH:

At 200, the UE transmits a PRACH preamble using separate PRACH resources for AI/ML-based random access procedures.

At 202, the gNB sends a RAR to the UE, which may include a timing reservation (TIMING ADVANCE, TA) and uplink authentication for scheduling Msg 3.

At 204, after adjusting the uplink timing, the UE transmits Msg3, msg3 comprising an L2/L3 message and a predicted beam report according to the UE side AI/ML model.

At 206, the gNB sends Msg4, which includes a contention resolution message and a TCI status update.

In one example, the paging message may include a request for CSI reports associated with the RACH procedure.

In another example, in Msg3, the predicted beam report may include beam information of the first K predicted beams (where K is an integer) and/or Layer 1reference signal received power (Layer 1reference signal received power,L1-RSRP). The higher layers may predefine or configure the value of K via RMSI, OSI, or RRC signaling.

In one example, the beam report may include an indication of whether the reported beam information is based on a prediction or measurement of the AI/ML model.

In another example, a TCI field may be included in DCI scheduling the Msg4 PDSCH. In this case, the RS resource index of the configured DL RS resource set for beam prediction may be included in DCI format 0_0 scrambled with a temporary Cell radio network temporary identifier (TC-RNTI).

In another example, when the value of K is 1, the UE may transmit the beam index of the best predicted beam and/or L1-RSRP in Msg 3. In this case, the gNB may use the beam index for scheduling transmission of PDCCH of Msg4 and Msg4 PDSCH. In this case, the TCI field may not appear in the TC-RNTI scrambled DCI format 0_0.

In another example, after the UE transmits the first K predicted beam information in Msg3, the gNB may transmit PDCCHs scheduling Msg4 and Msg4 PDSCH using the best predicted beam index with the highest L1-RSRP. In this case, the TCI field may not appear in the TC-RNTI scrambled DCI format 0_0.

Fig. 3 illustrates the steps one or more of which may be included in an AI/ML based random access procedure for a 2-step RACH.

At 300, the UE transmits MSGA PRACH and MsgA PUSCH using separate PRACH resources for AI/ML based random access procedures, the MsgA PUSCH including a predicted beam report according to the UE-side AI/ML model.

At 302, the gNB sends MsgB for success RAR (successRAR), the MsgB including a contention resolution message and a TCI status update.

In one example, in MsgA PUSCH, the predicted beam report may include beam information of the first K predicted beams and/or Layer 1reference signal received power (Layer 1reference signal received power,L1-RSRP). The higher layers may configure the value of K via RMSI, OSI, RRC signaling.

In one example, the UE may include an indication in the beam report to indicate whether the reported beam information is based on a prediction of the AI/ML model or based on measurements.

In another example, success RAR (successRAR) or rollback RAR (fallbackRAR) in MsgB PDSCH may include a TCI field. In this case, the RS resource index of the configured DL RS resource set for beam prediction may be included in success RAR (successRAR) or backoff RAR (fallbackRAR) in MsgB PDSCH.

In another example, when the value of K is 1, the UE may send the index of the best predicted beam and/or its L1-RSRP (predicted or measured) in MsgA PUSCH. In this case, the gNB may use the index of the best predicted beam for PDCCH and PDSCH transmissions, which occurs after MsgB and before RRC (re) configuration for TCI state. In this case, the TCI field may not appear in success RAR (successRAR) or rollback RAR (fallbackRAR) of MsgB PDSCH.

In another example, after the UE transmits the first K predicted beam information in MsgA PUSCH, the gNB may transmit PDCCH and PDSCH using the reported beam index, which occurs after MsgB and before RRC (re) configuration for TCI state. In this case, the TCI field may not appear in success RAR (successRAR) or rollback RAR (fallbackRAR) of MsgB PDSCH.

In an embodiment, RACH occasions (RACH occasions, RO) are configured to the UE via a system information (systeminformation, SI) message such that RO corresponds to DL Tx beams, which are identified as beams in beam set a. Thus, the configuration may include a mapping from DL RSs (such as CSI-RSs) and/or SSB resources to different ROs. Thus, RO selection of the UE indicates the corresponding DL Tx beam for the BS, as described in the following embodiments.

In a further example, the RO set may be configured by extending the SSB to RO mapping (as specified in NR and used for non-AI/ML based random access) to include additional ROs mapped to the corresponding DL Tx beams.

In another example, the RO set may be configured separately from the SSB-to-RO mapping (for non-AI/ML based random access) and may include (a) ROs mapped to configured SSBs, and (b) ROs mapped to other beams in beam set a (identified by DL RS resources, such as CSI-RS resources).

In implementation, the UE is expected to predict the best DL Tx beam and select RO accordingly to transmit Msg1 and Msg3 (for 4-step RACH) or MsgA (for 2-step RACH) using the corresponding Tx beam indicating the predicted best DL Tx beam for the BS. Thus, either Msg2/4 (for 4-step RACH) or MsgB (for 2-step RACH) can be transmitted using the indicated best DL Tx beam without further TCI status update indication.

In an embodiment, to ensure that network side conditions remain consistent when used for training and reasoning of the UE side AI/ML model, the BS provides one or more association IDs via broadcast (e.g., system information) or unicast (dedicated RRC signaling) as part of the configuration of beam set B and beam set a. The association ID may be provided to the set of beams or to each beam identified within the set of configured beams for measurement or for prediction.

In an embodiment, when the UE is in RRC connected mode, DL RS and/or SSB corresponding to beam set B (i.e., the beam set input as AI/ML model) and beam set a (i.e., the candidate beam set for model prediction) may be transmitted to the UE to generate training data for the UE-side AI/ML model. Any association ID may also be provided to the UE as part of the above configuration to facilitate collection of training data for the UE-side AI/ML model.

Random access procedure based on AI/ML of network

An embodiment of the network side AI/ML based random access procedure is provided as follows.

In an embodiment, for the network side AI/ML model for the random access procedure, the UE may send the beam information (including index) and/or L1-RSRP of the first N (N is an integer) measurement beams in Msg3 of the 4-step RACH procedure or MsgA PUSCH of the 2-step RACH procedure, respectively. The higher layers may configure the value of N via RMSI, OSI, or RRC signaling.

In an embodiment, for the network side AI/ML model for the random access procedure, the TCI field may be included in DCI of scheduling Msg4 PDSCH of the 4-step RACH or successRAR or fallbackRAR of MsgB PDSCH of the 2-step RACH, respectively. In this case, the RS resource index of the configured DL RS resource set for beam prediction may be included in DCI format 0_0 scrambled with a temporary Cell radio network temporary identifier (TC-RNTI) for the 4-step RACH or successRAR or fallbackRAR of MsgB PDSCH for the 2-step RACH, respectively.

In one example, when the value of N is 1, the UE may transmit the beam index and/or L1-RSRP of the best measurement beam in the Msg3 PUSCH of the 4-step RACH or in MsgA PUSCH of the 2-step RACH, respectively. In this case, the gNB may transmit PDCCH of the 4-step RACH scheduling Msg4 and Msg4 PDSCH using a beam index or PDCCH and PDSCH of the 2-step RACH using a beam index, which occurs after MsgB and before RRC (re) configuration for TCI state. In this case, the TCI field may not appear in the TC-RNTI scrambled DCI format 0_0 for the 4-step RACH or in the success RAR (successRAR) or the backoff RAR (fallbackRAR) of MsgB PDSCH for the 2-step RACH.

In another example, after the UE transmits the first K measurement beam information in Msg3, the gNB may transmit PDCCH for scheduling Msg4 and Msg4 PDSCH of the 4-step RACH using the reported beam index or PDCCH and PDSCH of the 2-step RACH using the reported beam index, which occurs after MsgB and before RRC (re) configuration for TCI state. In this case, the TCI field may not appear in DCI format 0_0 scrambled by TC-RNTI for the 4-step RACH, or successRAR or fallbackRA of MsgB PDSCH for the 2-step RACH.

Example procedure

Fig. 4 schematically illustrates the process described herein. The process may include or be related to a method performed by the UE, one or more elements of the UE, and/or one or more electronic devices that include and/or implement the UE. The process may include generating one or more predicted values related to a beam to be transmitted by the BS based on an AI/ML model at 401, wherein the one or more predicted values are related to a RACH procedure, transmitting a beam report to the BS, wherein the beam report includes the one or more predicted values at 402, identifying a contention resolution message including a TCI state update, wherein the contention resolution message is from the BS, and based on the beam report, at 403.

Fig. 5 schematically illustrates another process described herein. The process of fig. 5 may include or be associated with a method performed by a BS, one or more elements of a BS, and/or one or more electronic devices including and/or in a real BS. The process may include identifying a beam report containing one or more predictors related to the RACH procedure, wherein the beam report is received from a UE, the one or more predictors being generated by the UE based on an AI/ML model, at 501, transmitting a contention resolution message to the UE, wherein the contention resolution message includes a TCI status update, and based on the beam report, at 502.

Various networks, systems, devices, components are provided below that may implement aspects of the embodiments herein.

Network, component, and embodiment

Fig. 6 illustrates a network 600, which may implement some embodiments of the present disclosure. Network 600 may operate in a manner consistent with 3GPP technical specifications for LTE or 5G/NR systems.

The network 600 may include UEs 602, which may include any mobile or non-mobile computing device designed to communicate with the RAN 604 via a wireless connection. The UE 602 may be communicatively coupled with a RAN 604.

In an embodiment, the network 600 may include a plurality of UEs directly coupled to each other via a side link interface. The UE may be a Machine-to-Machine (M2M)/Device-to-Device (D2D) Device that communicates using a physical side Channel, such as, but not limited to, a physical side link broadcast Channel (PHYSICAL SIDELINK Broadcast Channel, PSBCH), a physical side link Downlink Channel (PHYSICAL SIDELINK Downlink Channel, PSDCH), and the like.

In an embodiment, the UE 602 may additionally communicate with an Access Point (AP) 606 via a wireless connection. The AP 606 may manage wireless local area network (Wireless Local Area Network, WLAN) connections that may be used to offload some/all network traffic from the RAN 604. The connection between the UE 602 and the AP 606 may conform to the 802.11 protocol of any Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) of ELECTRICAL AND Electronics Engineers

RAN 604 may include one or more Access nodes, such as AN Access Network (AN) 608.AN 608 may terminate the air interface protocol for UE 602 by providing AN access Layer protocol, which may be, for example, RRC, packet data convergence protocol (PACKET DATA Convergence Protocol, PDCP), radio link control (Radio Link Control, RLC), medium access control (Medium Access Control, MAC), and Layer 1 (Layer 1, l 1) protocols. In this way, the AN 608 may implement a data/voice connection between the CN 620 and the UE 602. In some embodiments, AN 608 may be implemented in a separate device or as part of one or more software entities running on a server computer as, for example, a virtual network. AN 608 may be referred to as a BS, a gNB, etc.

RAN 604 is communicatively coupled to CN 620, which includes network elements that provide various functions to support data and telecommunications services to clients/users (e.g., user UE 602). The components of Core Network (CN) 620 may be implemented in a single physical node or in multiple separate physical nodes.

In some embodiments, CN 620 may be LTE CN 622, which may also be referred to as evolved packet core (Evolved Packet Core, EPC). The 5GC 640 may include an authentication server function (Authentication Server Function, AUSF) 642, an access and mobility management function (ACCESS AND Mobility Management Function AMF) 644, a session management function (Session Management Function, SMF) 646, a user plane function (User Plane Function, UPF) 648, a network slice selection function (Network Slice Selection Function, NSSF) 650, a network opening function (Network Exposure Function, NEF) 652, a network storage function (Network Repository Function, NRF) 654, a policy control function (Policy Control Function, PCF) 656, a Unified data management (Unified DATA MANAGEMENT, UDM) 658, and an application function (Application Function, AF) 660 coupled to each other as shown.

The Data Network (DN) 636 can represent various network operator services, internet access, or third party services that can be provided by one or more servers (including, for example, application/content server 638).

Fig. 7 schematically illustrates a wireless network 700 in accordance with various embodiments. The wireless network 700 may include a UE 702 in wireless communication with AN 704. The UE 702 and the AN 704 may be similar to, and substantially interchangeable with, the components of the same name described elsewhere herein.

Fig. 10 schematically illustrates a simplified block diagram example of AI-assisted communication between a UE 1005 and a RAN 1010, in accordance with some embodiments of the disclosure. More specifically, as described in further detail below, the AI/ML model can be employed or utilized to facilitate wireless communication between the UE 1005 and the RAN 1010.

One or both of the UE 1005 and the RAN 1010 may operate in a manner consistent with 3GPP technical specifications or 6G system technical reports. In some embodiments, wireless cellular communication between UE 1005 and RAN 1010 may be part of network 900, network 600, and/or some other network described herein or operate concurrently with network 900, network 600, and/or some other network described herein.

UE 1005 may be similar to UE 902, UE 602, and/or some other UE described herein or share one or more features with UE 902, UE 602, and/or some other UE described herein. RAN 1010 may be similar to RAN 614, RAN 908, and/or some other RAN described herein, or share one or more features with RAN 614, RAN 908, and/or some other RAN described herein.

As can be seen in fig. 10, AI-related elements of UE 1005 may be similar to AI-related elements of RAN 1010. For purposes of discussion herein, descriptions of the various elements will be provided from the point of view of the UE 1005, but it should be understood that such discussion or description may be for identically named/numbered elements of the RAN 1010 unless explicitly stated otherwise.

As previously explained, the UE 1005 may include various elements or functions related to AI/ML. Such elements may be implemented as hardware, software, firmware, and/or some combination thereof.

One such element may be a data store 1015. The data store 1015 may be responsible for data collection and storage. In particular, the data store 1015 may collect and store RAN configuration parameters, measurement data, key performance indicators (key performance indicators, KPIs), model performance indicators, and the like, for model training, updating, and reasoning. More generally, the collected data is stored in a repository. The stored data can be discovered and retrieved by other elements of the data store 1015. For example, as can be seen, the inference data selection/filtering element 1050 can read data from the data store 1015. In various embodiments, the UE 1005 may be configured to discover and request data from a data store 1015 in the RAN, and vice versa. More generally, the data store 1015 of the UE 1005 may be communicatively coupled with the data store 1015 of the RAN 1010 such that the respective data stores of the UE and the RAN may share the collected data.

Another such element may be a training data selection/filtering function block 1020. Training data selection/filtering function block 1020 may be configured to generate training, validation, and test data sets for model training. Training data may be extracted from the data store 1015. The data may be selected/filtered based on the particular AI/ML model to be trained. The data may optionally be transformed/enhanced/preprocessed (e.g., normalized) before being loaded into the data set. The training data selection/filtering function 1020 may annotate the data in the dataset for supervised learning. The resulting data set may then be fed into a model training function block 1025 to train the model.

As described above, another such element may be model training function block 1025. This function block may be responsible for training and updating (retraining) the AI/ML model. The selected model may be trained (including training, validation, testing) using the fed-in data set from training data selection/filtering function block 1020. Model training function block 1025 may generate trained and tested deployment-ready AI/ML models. The trained and tested models may be stored in model store 1035.

Model repository 1035 may be responsible for the storage and opening of trained/untrained AI/ML models. The trained/updated model may be stored in model store 1035. The model and model parameters may be discovered and requested by other functional blocks (e.g., training data selection/filtering block 1020 and/or model training block 1025). In some embodiments, the UE 1005 may discover and request AI/ML models from the model repository 1035 of the RAN 1010. Similarly, the RAN 1010 may be capable of discovering and/or requesting AI/ML models from the model store 1035 of the UE 1005. In some embodiments, the RAN 1010 may configure the models and/or model parameters in the model store 1035 of the UE 1005.

Another such element may be a model management function block 1040. The model management function 1040 may be responsible for managing the AI/ML model generated by the model training function 1025. Such management functions may include deploying trained models, monitoring model performance, and the like. In model deployment, the model management function 1040 may allocate and schedule hardware and/or software resources for reasoning based on the received trained and tested models. As used herein, "inference" refers to the process of using a trained AI/ML model to generate data analytics, actions, policies, and the like based on input inference data. In performance monitoring, based on wireless KPIs and model performance metrics, the model management function 1040 may decide to terminate the running model, begin model retraining, select another model, etc. In an embodiment, the model management function 1040 of the RAN 1010 may configure the model management policies in the UE 1005 as shown.

Another such element may be an inference data selection/filtering function 1050. The inference data selection/filtering function 1050 may be responsible for generating a dataset for model inference at the inference function 1045, as described below. In particular, the inference data can be extracted from the data store 1015. The inference data selection/filtering function block 1050 may select and/or filter data based on the deployed AI/ML model. The data may be transformed/enhanced/preprocessed with the same flow as described with reference to block 1020. The resulting inference data set may be fed into an inference function block 1045.

Another such element may be an inference function 1045. The inference function 1045 may be responsible for performing the inferences described above. In particular, the inference function block 1045 may invoke the inference data set provided by the inference data selection/filtering function block 1050 and generate one or more results. Such results may be or include data analysis, actions, policies, and the like. The results may be provided to a performance measurement function 1030.

The performance measurement function 1030 may be configured to measure model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy, model bias, runtime delay, etc.) of the models that have been deployed and are executing based on the inference results for monitoring purposes. Model performance data may be stored in a data store 1015.
